entries.name: Tibetan gazelle
behaviour: upright at dawn on plateau grass; flushes by bunching and bounding
holds territories loosely around winter grass
distinguished from chiru by smaller build and lyrate horns

voxel_model.pattern: tawny upperparts, white belly and rump fan, heart-shaped horns (males)

entries.notes: The everyman gazelle of the Tibetan plateau; hunting pressure keeps numbers low below 5000 m. A mid-sized, readable prey animal for high-cold maps.

entries.name: Himalayan marmot
behaviour: hibernates through seven months of snow
sits bolt upright in colonies on plateau grassland
digging churns the soil into terraced mound fields

voxel_model.pattern: rufous and yellow-buff frosted coat

entries.notes: The plateau's largest squirrel and the main prey of eagles; marmot gall has been a valued medicine across the plateau for centuries.

entries.name: Plateau pika
behaviour: stores haypiles for winter instead of hibernating
forages at dawn and late afternoon, vanishing silently into burrows
colonies turn plateau grassland into pocked turf

voxel_model.pattern: small round body, no visible tail, rounded ears

entries.notes: The keystone species of the whole plateau grassland food web; herders poison them, predators depend on them. Model as scattered colonies, not singles.

entries.name: White-tailed prairie dog
behaviour: whistles from coterie mounds; white tail flashes when it dives
shares burrow towns with burrowing owls and black-footed ferrets
hibernates through the cold season at elevation

voxel_model.pattern: buff coat, white-tipped tail flag

entries.notes: The Great Basin's burrowing architect; towns are living terrain the player learns to avoid striding across.

entries.name: Brandt's vole
behaviour: tunnels mulched runways across overgrazed pasture
breeds explosively in plague years then crashes
eaten constantly by anything with a beak or a cat-like face

voxel_model.pattern: brown-backed, pale-bellied, short tail, small ears

entries.notes: The Gobi's background rodent; in plague years its runways cover the pasture and every raptor fattens.

entries.name: Mongolian gerbil
behaviour: family groups share deep burrow systems with many mouths
foot-drums in alarm
ancestor of nearly every lab gerbil in the world

voxel_model.pattern: sandy agouti back, pale belly, semi-tuft tail

entries.notes: The species behind the lab-gerbil stereotype; in the wild it is the desert's metronome, drumming at every disturbance.

entries.name: Djungarian hamster
behaviour: moults to a white winter coat with a grey dorsal stripe
huddles in burrow groups through deep cold
torpor lets it survive nights far below freezing

voxel_model.pattern: winter white with dark dorsal stripe

entries.notes: The Siberian winter specialist; its two snow-season colour phases are the kind of detail that sells seasonal world switches.

entries.name: Chisel-toothed kangaroo rat
behaviour: hops bipedally across sage flats at night
gnaws greasewood and sage with chisel-edged incisors
caches seed in larder burrows it digs itself

voxel_model.pattern: buff, hopping on elongated hind legs, long tufted tail

entries.notes: The Great Basin's hopping silhouette; sighting one under moonlight is the sagebrush equivalent of a kangaroo encounter.

entries.name: Sagebrush vole
behaviour: clips runways under sagebrush cover
stays low and grey, hard to spot against dusty shrubs
population pulses follow sage seed crops

voxel_model.pattern: grey-drab, blunt head, very short tail

entries.notes: A quiet vole for the sage belt; mostly noticed as the small prey item a kestrel is carrying.

entries.name: Siberian five-toed jerboa
behaviour: hops on elongated hind feet like a tiny kangaroo
freezes flat when lit, nearly invisible in moonlight
hibernates deeply in silty burrows

voxel_model.pattern: buff above, white below, very long tufted tail

entries.notes: The classic jerboa silhouette of Gobi night drives; upright ears and a tail three times the body are instantly readable at range.

entries.name: Long-eared jerboa
behaviour: earns its name: ears approach body length
kangaroo-hops between shrub shadows
one of the signature animals of the Taklamakan dunes

voxel_model.pattern: ears outsized, tail tip black-and-white plume

entries.notes: The Taklamakan's strangest charismatic rodent; ears like a rabbit on a body the size of a thumb.

entries.name: Plateau zokor
behaviour: lives almost entirely underground like a mole
barely functional eyes, broad flat snout for pushing soil
turns plateau turf into ridged diggings

voxel_model.pattern: silky chocolate fur, shovel claws, no tail

entries.notes: The Tibetan plateau's mole; almost never seen above ground. A digging-game dev would love it: tunnels as terrain, not sprites.

entries.name: Plains viscacha
behaviour: lives in colony 'vizcacheras' of interconnected burrows
sits out at night on haunches like a chinchilla on stilts
winks huge orange eyes at predators

voxel_model.pattern: long whiskers, grey-brown speckles, bushy tail

entries.notes: Patagonia's oversized chinchilla colony-builder; the vizcachera mound is a landmark a player can investigate at dusk.

entries.name: Big hairy armadillo (peludo)
behaviour: digs a bolt-hole in seconds when startled
whiskered face above a plated carapace with long hair between bands
burrows are used by other species afterward

voxel_model.pattern: banded carapace with hair poking between scutes

entries.notes: The most widespread armadillo south of the tropics; a genuinely surprising Patagonian spawn for players expecting only guanacos.

entries.name: Pallid bat
behaviour: lands on the ground to stalk scorpions, almost unique among bats
colonies hang in rocky roosts by day
large pale ears hear prey walking in sand

voxel_model.pattern: pale cream wings and snout, big donkey ears

entries.notes: A bat that hunts like a meerkat; the ultimate desert crack-wall ambience at dusk.

entries.name: Spotted bat
entries.migrates: may commute long foraging distances between roosts
behaviour: one of North America's most jeweled bats: black with three large white spots
huge pink ears and pinkish membrane flash in lamplight
roosts alone on cliff faces far above towns and light

voxel_model.pattern: three white dorsal spots, long pink ears

entries.notes: A hidden gem of the American west; nearly any cliff in the Great Basin could host one. Pure rarity-fuel for cave exploration.

entries.name: Ruddy shelduck
entries.migrates: strong and regular migrant between Central Asia and South Asia
behaviour: hoarse whistle carries over steppe wetlands
breeds far from water in rocky holes and ruins
pairs are fiercely territorial on nesting cliffs

voxel_model.pattern: russet body, cream head, black bill, white wing flash

entries.notes: The flame of steppe lakes and high plateau wetlands; its shrieking pair-call is the sound of every Gobi wetland scene. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Lesser kestrel
entries.migrates: migrates from Europe and Central Asia to tropical Africa
behaviour: gregarious; nests colonially in old buildings and cliffs
hunts over grazed steppe by day with trembling hover
deepest pied-black male plumage of all kestrels

voxel_model.pattern: males unbarred chestnut wings; females barred rufous

entries.notes: The kestrel of colonial ruins in Central Asia; where the game has an old mud-brick desert town, a colony should shriek above it. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Prairie falcon
entries.migrates: partial; northern birds slip south in winter
behaviour: sand devil of the Great Basin; stoops over sage flats
nests on bare cliff ledges hundreds of feet above ground
fades perfectly into dusty cliff limestone

voxel_model.pattern: sandy back, streaked whitish breast, dark cheek

entries.notes: The peregrine's pale cousin; every basalt bluff in the Great Basin seems to have one pair glaring down. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Ferruginous hawk
entries.migrates: northern populations winter south of the snowline
behaviour: largest hawk of open country; legs feathered to toes
hovers low over grass then stoops into prey
builds huge stick nests reused for years

voxel_model.pattern: rufous shoulders and leggings, whitish belly

entries.notes: The great eagle of the sage; the one hawk that feels big when seen sitting on a telegraph pole. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Long-legged buzzard
entries.migrates: partial migrant; northern birds winter in the Sahel and India
behaviour: stands eagle-like on a distant hillock scanning for rodents
often mixes into steppe eagle soaring flocks on migration
variable plumage from near-white to dark chocolate

voxel_model.pattern: rusty-buff below, dark trailing edge to wing, pale morph common

entries.notes: The default soaring raptor of Central Asian empty country; most distant eagle-shaped speck on the horizon. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Little owl
behaviour: day-active where undisturbed, bobbing on fenceposts and ruins
white scut-like eyebrows give a perpetually grumpy look
breeds in ground holes, wells and mud-brick walls

voxel_model.pattern: mottled brown-white, bold white brows, spotted crown

entries.notes: The ruin-and-well owl of Central Asia; a grumpy pair in every abandoned karez and mud-brick ruin. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Pallas's gull
entries.migrates: winters on the Indian Ocean and the Gulf
behaviour: bold black hood with white eye-crescents in summer
colonies on islands of steppe soda lakes
omnivorous swaggering presence around caravan wells

voxel_model.pattern: black hood, pale grey wings, white head in winter

entries.notes: The gull that owns steppe lakes thousands of kilometres from any sea; a colony is visible from a day's ride away. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Tibetan ground tit
behaviour: hops on the ground like a miniature crow
endemic to the Tibetan plateau, living near marmot and zokor burrows
cooperative family groups defend territories against foxes and eagles

voxel_model.pattern: sand-buff above, dark wings, pale throat barred dark

entries.notes: A bird that looks like a fluffed-up ground jay and lives only on the high plateau; one of those endemics that makes a plateau map feel real. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: White-winged snowfinch
behaviour: flashes big white wing-patches when flushed
breeds in rodent burrows and cliff crevices
often joins snowfinch flocks on high pastures

voxel_model.pattern: grey-brown above, white wings with black tips, dark moustachial stripe

entries.notes: The high-altitude sparrow of cold rock; a flock rising off a scree slope all-white against brown stone. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Isabelline wheatear
behaviour: sits upright on a burrow mound or stone for long periods
nests deep in rodent burrows, dropping like a stone into the hole
ash-buff overall; the classic wheatear of flat empty country

voxel_model.pattern: uniform sandy-buff, black tail with white base

entries.notes: The upright sentinel of every Gobi track; learns humans stop hunting it and watches very closely. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Asian desert warbler
behaviour: long graduated tail cocked and fanned in song flights
one of the few warblers truly at home in the Gobi and Taklamakan
monotonous trilling from low desert scrub at dawn

voxel_model.pattern: grey-brown above, pale below, rusty rump

entries.notes: Proof that even the harshest sand has a resident singer; background audio for dune ridges. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Henderson's ground jay
behaviour: jet-black crow-like bird with an elegant crest and pale tail
runs rather than flies across open dune and gravel
one of the signature endemics of Gobi expeditions

voxel_model.pattern: black body, white outer tail, scarlet wing flash, thin crest

entries.notes: A crow that chose the desert; Pallas and Przewalski both wrote home about it. The single most Gobi-specific bird in this file. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Russian (Horsfield's) tortoise
behaviour: four claws per foot, not five — a classic field mark
brumates in deep burrows through bitter steppe winters
sprints surprisingly fast for a tortoise when needed

voxel_model.pattern: round domed shell, ochre with dark blotches

entries.notes: The only tortoise that truly brackets Mongolian cold; a charismatic slow-moving pick-up-and-carry for desert players.

entries.name: Halys pit viper
entries.migrates: brumates communally in rock dens through winter
behaviour: the commonest Central Asian viper; a steppe pit viper
live-bearing; dens with dozens of snakes in October
strikes fast with haemolytic venom when stepped on

voxel_model.pattern: brown with dark transverse bars and a pale stripe behind the eye

entries.notes: The desert-edge snake of the Gobi fringe; a genuine cold-adapted viper, not a Sonoran import. Respect it in rock dens.

entries.name: Midget faded rattlesnake
entries.migrates: brumates communally with other rattlesnakes in basalt dens
behaviour: small, bleached-out rattler of canyon country
fades to straw in desert-wash populations
rattles faintly, leaving an inattentive hiker to walk on

voxel_model.pattern: faded diamond blotches on straw ground

entries.notes: The faded ghost rattler of the canyonlands; smaller and more secretive than its Great Basin cousin.

entries.name: Long-nosed leopard lizard
behaviour: sprints from ambush like a small theropod
spots and blotches flash on raised alert
cannibalises other lizards when insects are scarce

voxel_model.pattern: spotted reticulum on buff, white-ringed eyespots on tail

entries.notes: The Great Basin's pocket dinosaur; dashes between sagebrush across bare washes.

entries.name: Desert horned lizard
behaviour: horned toad; flattens into the sand and vanishes
specialist ant-eater with horned cranial armour
can squirt blood from its eyes at persistent predators

voxel_model.pattern: fringed scales, crown of head spines, two long tail-pointed blotches

entries.notes: A living stone with horns; the eyeblood defence is real and unforgettable the first time it happens near you.

entries.name: Common leopard gecko
behaviour: the archetypal pet gecko, a Gobi-fringe native
fat tails store reserves for lean seasons
moves with jerky gecko gaits under stones by night

voxel_model.pattern: bold dark blotches on straw, segmented fat tail

entries.notes: The gecko every player recognises from pet shops, out in its wild dry hill country, clucking from under rocks.

entries.name: Great Basin spadefoot toad
behaviour: explosive breeder: emerges after desert rain to fill temporary pools
spade on each hind foot for digging backward into sand
tadpoles can metamorphose in as little as two weeks

voxel_model.pattern: smooth olive-dusted skin, vertical pupils, yellowish dorsal stripe

entries.notes: The desert that explodes with frog song after one inch of rain; the spadefoot is the payoff for players who wait out storms.

entries.name: Mormon cricket
entries.migrates: periodic marching swarms across ranges and highways
behaviour: flightless; swarms march wingless in fronts miles wide
name comes from the 1848 cricket plague on Mormon pioneer crops — supposedly ended by seagulls
clicks loudly by rubbing wings

voxel_model.pattern: black warty shield, orange-red shoulders in some forms

entries.notes: Not a cricket and not a locust but a katydid relative; if the game ever wants a biblical swarm set piece in the Great Basin, this is it.

entries.name: Painted lady
entries.migrates: intercontinental; Gobi swarms reach Europe in irruptive years
behaviour: most widespread butterfly on Earth
irruptions in the Gobi can darken the sky for days
gardens its life in thistle clumps along tracks

voxel_model.pattern: orange with black spots and white wing-tips

entries.notes: The butterfly whose migrations rival bird flights; an utterly convincing ambient swarm after good rain years.

entries.name: Western black widow
behaviour: messy irregular cobwebs in clutter, woodpiles and sheds
females jet-black with hourglass; males tiny and streaked
reclusive; bites humans only when web-pressed

voxel_model.pattern: glossy black sphere, red hourglass beneath

entries.notes: A genuinely dangerous roommate of every Great Basin woodpile; worth a warning sign on sheds in the game's loot pool.

entries.name: Devils Hole pupfish
behaviour: exists nowhere on Earth except a single limestone cave shaft in Nevada
survives in water hotter and more saline than almost any fish's tolerance
total population has dipped below 50 individuals

voxel_model.pattern: small blue-sheened flanks, males with black fins and metallic blue

entries.notes: The most range-restricted vertebrate alive; a natural end-of-game pilgrimage for conservation-aware players — and a cautionary tale in one flooded desert cavern.

entries.name: Lahontan cutthroat trout
entries.migrates: spawning runs up cold desert streams in spring
behaviour: native trout of the ancient Lake Lahontan basin
red slash under the jaw — the cutthroat mark
survives only in a handful of protected Great Basin streams

voxel_model.pattern: olive back, dense small spots, crimson throat slash

entries.notes: The only native salmonid of the Great Basin; catching one in a desert stream is a genuine event — this species should not be everywhere.
